rules.name: cpp/commented-out-code
rules.description: Commented-out code makes the remaining code more difficult to read.

rules.name: cpp/fixme-comment
rules.description: Comments containing 'FIXME' indicate that the code has known bugs.

rules.name: cpp/memset-may-be-deleted
rules.description: Using the `memset` function to clear private data in a variable that has no subsequent use can make information-leak vulnerabilities easier to exploit because the compiler can remove the call.

rules.name: cpp/toctou-race-condition
rules.description: Separately checking the state of a file before operating on it may allow an attacker to modify the file between the two operations.

rules.name: cpp/uncontrolled-arithmetic
rules.description: Arithmetic operations on uncontrolled data that is not validated can cause overflows.

rules.name: cpp/comparison-with-wider-type
rules.description: Comparisons between types of different widths in a loop condition can cause the loop to behave unexpectedly.

rules.name: cpp/non-https-url
rules.description: Non-HTTPS connections can be intercepted by third parties.

rules.name: cpp/suspicious-add-sizeof
rules.description: Explicitly scaled pointer arithmetic expressions can cause buffer overflow conditions if the offset is also implicitly scaled.

rules.name: cpp/command-line-injection
rules.description: Using user-supplied data in an OS command, without neutralizing special elements, can make code vulnerable to command injection.

rules.name: cpp/cgi-xss
rules.description: Writing user input directly to a web page allows for a cross-site scripting vulnerability.

rules.name: cpp/unsafe-dacl-security-descriptor
rules.description: Setting a DACL to NULL in a SECURITY_DESCRIPTOR will result in an unprotected object. If the DACL that belongs to the security descriptor of an object is set to NULL, a null DACL is created. A null DACL grants full access to any user who requests it; normal security checking is not performed with respect to the object.

rules.name: cpp/open-call-with-mode-argument
rules.description: Opening a file with the O_CREAT flag but without mode argument reads arbitrary bytes from the stack.

rules.name: cpp/insufficient-key-size
rules.description: Using cryptographic algorithms with too small a key size can allow an attacker to compromise security.

rules.name: cpp/openssl-heartbleed
rules.description: Using an old version of OpenSSL can allow remote attackers to retrieve portions of memory.

rules.name: cpp/weak-cryptographic-algorithm
rules.description: Using broken or weak cryptographic algorithms can allow an attacker to compromise security.

rules.name: cpp/cleartext-transmission
rules.description: Transmitting sensitive information across a network in cleartext can expose it to an attacker.

rules.name: cpp/cleartext-storage-file
rules.description: Storing sensitive information in cleartext can expose it to an attacker.

rules.name: cpp/external-entity-expansion
rules.description: Parsing user-controlled XML documents and allowing expansion of external entity references may lead to disclosure of confidential data or denial of service.

rules.name: cpp/dangerous-cin
rules.description: Using `cin` without specifying the length of the input may be dangerous.

rules.name: cpp/dangerous-function-overflow
rules.description: Use of a standard library function that does not guard against buffer overflow.

rules.name: cpp/badly-bounded-write
rules.description: Buffer write operations with a length parameter that does not match the size of the destination buffer may overflow.

rules.name: cpp/very-likely-overrunning-write
rules.description: Buffer write operations that do not control the length of data written may overflow

rules.name: cpp/hresult-boolean-conversion
rules.description: Casting an HRESULT to/from a Boolean type and then using it in a test expression will yield an incorrect result because success (S_OK) in HRESULT is indicated by a value of 0.

rules.name: cpp/tainted-format-string
rules.description: Using externally-controlled format strings in printf-style functions can lead to buffer overflows or data representation problems.

rules.name: cpp/incorrect-string-type-conversion
rules.description: Casting a byte string to a wide-character string is likely to yield a string that is incorrectly terminated or aligned. This can lead to undefined behavior, including buffer overruns.

rules.name: cpp/unsigned-difference-expression-compared-zero
rules.description: A subtraction with an unsigned result can never be negative. Using such an expression in a relational comparison with `0` is likely to be wrong.

rules.name: cpp/system-data-exposure
rules.description: Exposing system data or debugging information helps a malicious user learn about the system and form an attack plan.

rules.name: cpp/iterator-to-expired-container
rules.description: Using an iterator owned by a container whose lifetime has expired may lead to unexpected behavior.

rules.name: cpp/use-of-string-after-lifetime-ends
rules.description: If the value of a call to 'c_str' outlives the underlying object it may lead to unexpected behavior.

rules.name: cpp/use-of-unique-pointer-after-lifetime-ends
rules.description: Referencing the contents of a unique pointer after the underlying object has expired may lead to unexpected behavior.

rules.name: cpp/no-space-for-terminator
rules.description: Allocating a buffer using 'malloc' without ensuring that there is always space for the entire string and a zero terminator can cause a buffer overrun.

rules.name: cpp/sql-injection
rules.description: Including user-supplied data in a SQL query without neutralizing special elements can make code vulnerable to SQL Injection.

rules.name: cpp/irregular-enum-init
rules.description: In an enumerator list, the = construct should not be used to explicitly initialize members other than the first, unless all items are explicitly initialized. An exception is the pattern to use the last element of an enumerator list to get the number of possible values.

rules.name: cpp/virtual-call-in-constructor
rules.description: Virtual functions should not be invoked from a constructor or destructor of the same class. Confusingly, virtual functions are resolved statically (not dynamically) in constructors and destructors for the same class. The call should be made explicitly static by qualifying it using the scope resolution operator.

rules.name: cpp/array-in-interface
rules.description: Arrays should not be used in interfaces. Arrays degenerate to pointers when passed as parameters. This array decay problem has long been known to be a source of errors. Consider using std::vector or encapsulating the array in an Array class.

rules.name: cpp/undisciplined-multiple-inheritance
rules.description: Multiple inheritance should only be used in the following restricted form: n interfaces plus m private implementations, plus at most one protected implementation. Multiple inheritance can lead to complicated inheritance hierarchies that are difficult to comprehend and maintain.

rules.name: cpp/assignment-does-not-return-this
rules.description: An assignment operator should return a reference to *this. Both the standard library types and the built-in types behave in this manner.

rules.name: cpp/redefined-default-parameter
rules.description: An inherited default parameter shall never be redefined. Default values are bound statically which is confusing when combined with dynamically bound function calls.

rules.name: cpp/resource-not-released-in-destructor
rules.description: All resources acquired by a class should be released by its destructor. Avoid the use of the 'open / close' pattern, since C++ constructors and destructors provide a safer way to handle resource acquisition and release. Best practice in C++ is to use the 'RAII' technique: constructors allocate resources and destructors free them.

rules.name: cpp/inconsistent-virtual-inheritance
rules.description: A base class shall not be both virtual and non-virtual in the same hierarchy.

rules.name: cpp/missing-header-guard
rules.description: Header files should contain header guards (#defines to prevent the file from being included twice). This prevents errors and inefficiencies caused by repeated inclusion.

rules.name: cpp/trivial-switch
rules.description: Using a switch statement when there are fewer than two non-default cases leads to unclear code.

rules.name: cpp/loop-variable-changed
rules.description: Numeric variables being used within a for loop for iteration counting should not be modified in the body of the loop. Reserve for loops for straightforward iterations, and use a while loop instead for more complex cases.

rules.name: cpp/loop-variable-float
rules.description: Floating point variables should not be used as loop counters. For loops are best suited to simple increments and termination conditions; while loops are preferable for more complex uses.

rules.name: cpp/sizeof-side-effect
rules.description: The sizeof operator should not be used on expressions that contain side effects. It is subtle whether the side effects will occur or not.

rules.name: cpp/missing-return
rules.description: All functions that are not void should return a value on every exit path.

rules.name: cpp/function-in-block
rules.description: Functions should always be declared at file scope. It is confusing to declare a function at block scope, and the visibility of the function is not what would be expected.

rules.name: cpp/include-non-header
rules.description: The #include pre-processor directive should only be used to include header files.

rules.name: cpp/use-of-goto
rules.description: The goto statement can make the control flow of a function hard to understand, when used for purposes other than error handling.

rules.name: cpp/complex-block
rules.description: Blocks with too many consecutive statements are candidates for refactoring. Only complex statements are counted here (eg. for, while, switch ...). The top-level logic will be clearer if each complex statement is extracted to a function.

rules.name: cpp/complex-condition
rules.description: Boolean expressions that are too deeply nested are hard to read and understand. Consider naming intermediate results as local variables.

rules.name: cpp/guarded-free
rules.description: NULL-condition guards before function calls to the memory-deallocation function free(3) are unnecessary, because passing NULL to free(3) is a no-op.

rules.name: cpp/slicing
rules.description: Assigning a non-reference instance of a derived type to a variable of the base type slices off all members added by the derived class, and can cause an unexpected state.

rules.name: cpp/empty-block
rules.description: An empty block after a conditional can be a sign of an omission and can decrease maintainability of the code. Such blocks should contain an explanatory comment to aid future maintainers.

rules.name: cpp/rethrow-no-exception
rules.description: When there is nothing to rethrow, attempting to rethrow an exception will terminate the program.

rules.name: cpp/throwing-pointer
rules.description: Exceptions should be objects rather than pointers to objects.

rules.name: cpp/catch-missing-free
rules.description: If an exception is allocated on the heap, then it should be deleted when caught.

rules.name: cpp/catch-by-value
rules.description: Catching an exception by value will create a copy of the thrown exception, thereby potentially slicing the original exception object.

rules.name: cpp/rule-of-two
rules.description: Classes that have an explicit copy constructor or copy assignment operator may behave inconsistently if they do not have both.

rules.name: cpp/long-switch
rules.description: A switch statement with too much code in its cases can make the control flow hard to follow. Consider wrapping the code for each case in a function and just using the switch statement to invoke the appropriate function in each case.

rules.name: cpp/short-global-name
rules.description: Global variables should have descriptive names, to help document their use, avoid namespace pollution and reduce the risk of shadowing with local variables.

rules.name: cpp/declaration-hides-variable
rules.description: A local variable hides another local variable from a surrounding scope. This may be confusing. Consider renaming one of the variables.

rules.name: cpp/local-variable-hides-global-variable
rules.description: A local variable or parameter that hides a global variable of the same name. This may be confusing. Consider renaming one of the variables.

rules.name: cpp/declaration-hides-parameter
rules.description: A local variable hides a parameter. This may be confusing. Consider renaming one of them.

rules.name: cpp/unused-local-variable
rules.description: A local variable that is never called or accessed may be an indication that the code is incomplete or has a typo.

rules.name: cpp/unused-static-variable
rules.description: A static variable that is never accessed may be an indication that the code is incomplete or has a typo.

rules.name: cpp/unused-static-function
rules.description: A static function that is never called or accessed may be an indication that the code is incomplete or has a typo.

rules.name: cpp/ambiguously-signed-bit-field
rules.description: Bit fields with integral types should have explicit signedness only. For example, use `unsigned int` rather than `int`. It is implementation specific whether an `int`-typed bit field is signed, so there could be unexpected sign extension or overflow.

rules.name: cpp/redundant-null-check-simple
rules.description: Checking a pointer for nullness after dereferencing it is likely to be a sign that either the check can be removed, or it should be moved before the dereference.

rules.name: cpp/unsafe-use-of-this
rules.description: A call to a pure virtual function using a 'this' pointer of an object that is under construction may lead to undefined behavior.

rules.name: cpp/throw-in-destructor
rules.description: Throwing an exception from a destructor may cause immediate program termination.

rules.name: cpp/constructor-delegation
rules.description: A constructor in C++ cannot delegate part of the object initialization to another by calling it. This is likely to leave part of the object uninitialized.

rules.name: cpp/virtual-destructor
rules.description: All base classes with a virtual function should define a virtual destructor. If an application attempts to delete a derived class object through a base class pointer, the result is undefined if the base class destructor is non-virtual.

rules.name: cpp/upcast-array-pointer-arithmetic
rules.description: An array with elements of a derived struct type is cast to a pointer to the base type of the struct. If pointer arithmetic or an array dereference is done on the resulting pointer, it will use the width of the base type, leading to misaligned reads.

rules.name: cpp/implicit-bitfield-downcast
rules.description: A bitfield is implicitly downcast to a smaller integer type. This could lead to loss of upper bits of the bitfield.

rules.name: cpp/lossy-pointer-cast
rules.description: A pointer type is converted to a smaller integer type. This may lead to loss of information in the variable and is highly non-portable.

rules.name: cpp/array-arg-size-mismatch
rules.description: Finds function calls where the size of an array being passed is smaller than the array size of the declared parameter. This could lead to accesses to memory locations beyond the parameter's array bounds.

rules.name: cpp/return-stack-allocated-memory
rules.description: A function returns a pointer to a stack-allocated region of memory. This memory is deallocated at the end of the function, which may lead the caller to dereference a dangling pointer.

rules.name: cpp/using-expired-stack-address
rules.description: Accessing the stack-allocated memory of a function after it has returned can lead to memory corruption.

rules.name: cpp/return-c-str-of-std-string
rules.description: Returning the c_str of a locally allocated std::string could cause the program to crash or behave non-deterministically because the memory is deallocated when the std::string goes out of scope.

rules.name: cpp/unsafe-strncat
rules.description: Calling 'strncat' with an incorrect size argument may result in a buffer overflow.

rules.name: cpp/pointer-overflow-check
rules.description: Adding a value to a pointer to check if it overflows relies on undefined behavior and may lead to memory corruption.

rules.name: cpp/alloca-in-loop
rules.description: Using alloca in a loop can lead to a stack overflow

rules.name: cpp/useless-expression
rules.description: A pure expression whose value is ignored is likely to be the result of a typo.

rules.name: cpp/logical-operator-applied-to-flag
rules.description: A short-circuiting logical operator is applied to what looks like a flag. This may be a typo for a bitwise operator.

rules.name: cpp/dubious-null-check
rules.description: The address of a field (except the first) will never be NULL, so it is misleading, at best, to check for that case.

rules.name: cpp/compare-where-assign-meant
rules.description: The '==' operator may have been used accidentally, where '=' was intended, resulting in a useless test.

rules.name: cpp/string-copy-return-value-as-boolean
rules.description: The return value for strcpy, strncpy, or related string copy functions have no reserved return value to indicate an error. Using them in a condition is likely to be a logic error.

rules.name: cpp/inconsistent-loop-direction
rules.description: A for-loop iteration expression goes backward with respect of the initialization statement and condition expression.

rules.name: cpp/empty-if
rules.description: An if-statement with an empty then-branch and no else-branch may indicate that the code is incomplete.

rules.name: cpp/assign-where-compare-meant
rules.description: The '=' operator may have been used accidentally, where '==' was intended.

rules.name: cpp/constant-comparison
rules.description: When a comparison operation, such as x < y, always returns the same result, it means that the comparison is redundant and may mask a bug because a different check was intended.

rules.name: cpp/bad-addition-overflow-check
rules.description: Checking for overflow of integer addition by comparing against one of the arguments of the addition does not work when the result of the addition is automatically promoted to a larger type.

rules.name: cpp/comparison-precedence
rules.description: Using comparisons as operands of other comparisons is unusual in itself, and most readers will require parentheses to be sure of the precedence.

rules.name: cpp/integer-multiplication-cast-to-long
rules.description: A multiplication result that is converted to a larger type can be a sign that the result can overflow the type converted from.

rules.name: cpp/bitwise-sign-check
rules.description: Checking the sign of the result of a bitwise operation may yield unexpected results.

rules.name: cpp/unsigned-comparison-zero
rules.description: An unsigned value is always non-negative, even if it has been assigned a negative number, so the comparison is redundant and may mask a bug because a different check was intended.

rules.name: cpp/equality-on-floats
rules.description: Comparing results of floating-point computations with '==' or '!=' is likely to yield surprising results since floating-point computation does not follow the standard rules of algebra.

rules.name: cpp/signed-overflow-check
rules.description: Testing for overflow by adding a value to a variable to see if it "wraps around" works only for unsigned integer values.

rules.name: cpp/comparison-of-identical-expressions
rules.description: Comparing a variable to itself always produces the same result, unless the purpose is to check for integer overflow or floating point NaN.

rules.name: cpp/wrong-type-format-argument
rules.description: Calling a printf-like function with the wrong type of arguments causes unpredictable behavior.

rules.name: cpp/overflowing-snprintf
rules.description: Using the return value from snprintf without proper checks can cause overflow.

rules.name: cpp/non-constant-format
rules.description: Passing a value that is not a string literal 'format' string to a printf-like function can lead to a mismatch between the number of arguments defined by the 'format' and the number of arguments actually passed to the function. If the format string ultimately stems from an untrusted source, this can be used for exploits. This query finds format strings coming from non-literal sources. Note that format strings of type `const char*` it is still considered non-constant if the value is not coming from a string literal. For example, for a parameter with type `const char*` of an exported function that is used as a format string, there is no way to ensure the originating value was a string literal.

rules.name: cpp/too-many-format-arguments
rules.description: A printf-like function called with too many arguments will ignore the excess arguments and output less than might have been intended.

rules.name: cpp/wrong-number-format-arguments
rules.description: Calling a printf-like function with too few arguments can be a source of security issues.

rules.name: cpp/too-few-arguments
rules.description: A function call is passing fewer arguments than the number of declared parameters of the function. This may indicate that the code does not follow the author's intent. It is also a vulnerability, since the function is likely to operate on undefined data.

rules.name: cpp/implicit-function-declaration
rules.description: An implicitly declared function is assumed to take no arguments and return an integer. If this assumption does not hold, it may lead to unpredictable behavior.

rules.name: cpp/futile-params
rules.description: A function call to a function passed more arguments than there are declared parameters of the function. This may indicate that the code does not follow the author's intent.

rules.name: cpp/non-member-const-no-effect
rules.description: A 'const' modifier on a function return type is useless and should be removed for clarity.

rules.name: cpp/member-const-no-effect
rules.description: A 'const' modifier on a member function return type is useless. It is usually a typo or misunderstanding, since the syntax for a 'const' function is 'int foo() const', not 'const int foo()'.

rules.name: cpp/continue-in-false-loop
rules.description: A 'continue' statement only re-runs the loop if the loop-condition is true. Therefore using 'continue' in a loop with a constant false condition is misleading and usually a bug.

rules.name: cpp/use-in-own-initializer
rules.description: Loading from a variable in its own initializer may lead to undefined behavior.

rules.name: cpp/duplicate-include-guard
rules.description: Using the same include guard macro in more than one header file may cause unexpected behavior from the compiler.

rules.name: cpp/new-array-delete-mismatch
rules.description: An array allocated with 'new[]' is being freed using 'delete'. Behavior in such cases is undefined and should be avoided. Use 'delete[]' when freeing arrays allocated with 'new[]'.

rules.name: cpp/new-delete-array-mismatch
rules.description: An object that was allocated with 'new' is being freed using 'delete[]'. Behavior in such cases is undefined and should be avoided. Use 'delete' instead.

rules.name: cpp/incorrectly-checked-scanf
rules.description: Failing to account for EOF in a call to a scanf-like function can lead to undefined behavior.

rules.name: cpp/new-free-mismatch
rules.description: An object that was allocated with 'malloc' or 'new' is being freed using a mismatching 'free' or 'delete'.

rules.name: cpp/double-free
rules.description: Freeing a resource more than once can lead to undefined behavior and cause memory corruption.

rules.name: cpp/use-after-free
rules.description: An allocated memory block is used after it has been freed. Behavior in such cases is undefined and can cause memory corruption.

rules.name: cpp/large-parameter
rules.description: An object larger than 64 bytes is passed by value to a function. Passing large objects by value unnecessarily use up scarce stack space, increase the cost of calling a function and can be a security risk. Use a const pointer to the object instead.

rules.name: cpp/static-buffer-overflow
rules.description: Exceeding the size of a static array during write or access operations may result in a buffer overflow.

rules.name: cpp/dead-code-goto
rules.description: A goto or break statement is followed by unreachable code.

rules.name: cpp/poorly-documented-function
rules.description: Large functions that have no or almost no comments are likely to be too complex to understand and maintain. The larger a function is, the more problematic the lack of comments.

rules.name: cpp/overflow-buffer
rules.description: Incorrect use of a function that accesses a memory buffer may read or write data past the end of that buffer.

rules.name: cpp/overrun-write
rules.description: Exceeding the size of a static array during write or access operations may result in a buffer overflow.

rules.name: cpp/uncontrolled-allocation-size
rules.description: Allocating memory with a size controlled by an external user can result in arbitrary amounts of memory being allocated.

rules.name: cpp/suspicious-pointer-scaling
rules.description: Implicit scaling of pointer arithmetic expressions can cause buffer overflow conditions.

rules.name: cpp/suspicious-pointer-scaling-void
rules.description: Implicit scaling of pointer arithmetic expressions can cause buffer overflow conditions.

rules.name: cpp/certificate-not-checked
rules.description: Always check the result of certificate verification after fetching an SSL certificate.

rules.name: cpp/certificate-result-conflation
rules.description: Only accept SSL certificates that pass certificate verification.

rules.name: cpp/invalid-pointer-deref
rules.description: Dereferencing an out-of-bounds pointer is undefined behavior and may lead to security vulnerabilities.

rules.name: cpp/world-writable-file-creation
rules.description: Creating a file that is world-writable can allow an attacker to write to the file.

rules.name: cpp/cleartext-storage-buffer
rules.description: Storing sensitive information in cleartext can expose it to an attacker.

rules.name: cpp/path-injection
rules.description: Accessing paths influenced by users can allow an attacker to access unexpected resources.

rules.name: cpp/uncontrolled-process-operation
rules.description: Using externally controlled strings in a process operation can allow an attacker to execute malicious commands.

rules.name: cpp/potentially-dangerous-function
rules.description: Use of a standard library function that is not thread-safe.

rules.name: cpp/type-confusion
rules.description: Casting a value to an incompatible type can lead to undefined behavior.

rules.name: cpp/user-controlled-bypass
rules.description: Authentication by checking that the peer's address matches a known IP or web address is unsafe as it is vulnerable to spoofing attacks.

rules.name: cpp/unbounded-write
rules.description: Buffer write operations that do not control the length of data written may overflow.

rules.name: cpp/overrunning-write
rules.description: Buffer write operations that do not control the length of data written may overflow.

rules.name: cpp/overrunning-write-with-float
rules.description: Buffer write operations that do not control the length of data written may overflow when floating point inputs take extreme values.

rules.name: cpp/cleartext-storage-database
rules.description: Storing sensitive information in a non-encrypted database can expose it to an attacker.

rules.name: cpp/tainted-permissions-check
rules.description: Using untrusted inputs in a statement that makes a security decision makes code vulnerable to attack.

rules.name: cpp/potential-system-data-exposure
rules.description: Exposing sensitive system data helps a malicious user learn about the system and form an attack plan.

rules.name: cpp/incorrect-allocation-error-handling
rules.description: Mixing up the failure conditions of 'operator new' and 'operator new(std::nothrow)' can result in unexpected behavior.

rules.name: cpp/unsafe-create-process-call
rules.description: Calling a function of the CreateProcess* family of functions, where the path contains spaces, introduces a security vulnerability.

rules.name: cpp/unterminated-variadic-call
rules.description: Calling a variadic function without a sentinel value may result in a buffer overflow if the function expects a specific value to terminate the argument list.

rules.name: cpp/integer-used-for-enum
rules.description: Enumeration types should be used instead of integer types (and constants) to select from a limited series of choices.

rules.name: cpp/offset-use-before-range-check
rules.description: Accessing an array offset before checking the range means that the program may attempt to read beyond the end of a buffer

rules.name: cpp/comma-before-misleading-indentation
rules.description: If expressions before and after a comma operator use different indentation, it is easy to misread the purpose of the code.

rules.name: cpp/inconsistent-call-on-result
rules.description: A function is called, and the same operation is usually performed on the return value - for example, free, delete, close etc. However, in some cases it is not performed. These unusual cases may indicate misuse of the API and could cause resource leaks.

rules.name: cpp/lossy-function-result-cast
rules.description: Finds function calls whose result type is a floating point type, and which are casted to an integral type. Includes only expressions with implicit cast and excludes function calls to ceil, floor and round.

rules.name: cpp/suspicious-sizeof
rules.description: Taking 'sizeof' of an array parameter is often mistakenly thought to yield the size of the underlying array, but it always yields the machine pointer size.

rules.name: cpp/stack-address-escape
rules.description: Storing the address of a local variable in non-local memory can cause a dangling pointer bug if the address is used after the function returns.

rules.name: cpp/bad-strncpy-size
rules.description: Calling 'strncpy' with the size of the source buffer as the third argument may result in a buffer overflow.

rules.name: cpp/uninitialized-local
rules.description: Reading from a local variable that has not been assigned to will typically yield garbage.

rules.name: cpp/unsafe-strcat
rules.description: Using 'strcat' without checking the size of the source string may result in a buffer overflow

rules.name: cpp/inconsistent-null-check
rules.description: The result value of a function is often checked for nullness, but not always. Since the value is mostly checked, it is likely that the function can return null values in some cases, and omitting the check could crash the program.

rules.name: cpp/missing-case-in-switch
rules.description: A switch statement over an enum type is missing a case for some enum constant and does not have a default case. This may cause logic errors.

rules.name: cpp/incorrect-not-operator-usage
rules.description: Usage of a logical-not (!) operator as an operand for a bit-wise operation. This commonly indicates the usage of an incorrect operator instead of the bit-wise not (~) operator, also known as ones' complement operator.

rules.name: cpp/incomplete-parity-check
rules.description: Using "x % 2 == 1" to check whether x is odd does not work for negative numbers.

rules.name: cpp/nested-loops-with-same-variable
rules.description: When a nested loop uses the same iteration variable as its outer loop, the behavior of the outer loop easily becomes difficult to understand as the inner loop will affect its control flow. It is likely to be a typo.

rules.name: cpp/mistyped-function-arguments
rules.description: When the type of a function argument is not compatible with the type of the corresponding parameter, it may lead to unpredictable behavior.

rules.name: cpp/boost/tls-settings-misconfiguration
rules.description: Using the TLS or SSLv23 protocol from the boost::asio library, but not disabling deprecated protocols, or disabling minimum-recommended protocols.

rules.name: cpp/boost/use-of-deprecated-hardcoded-security-protocol
rules.description: Using a deprecated hard-coded protocol using the boost::asio library.

rules.name: cpp/leap-year/adding-365-days-per-year
rules.description: When an arithmetic operation modifies a date by a constant value of 365, it may be a sign that leap years are not taken into account.

rules.name: cpp/leap-year/unchecked-return-value-for-time-conversion-function
rules.description: When the return value of a fallible time conversion function is not checked for failure, its output parameters may contain invalid dates.

rules.name: cpp/leap-year/unchecked-after-arithmetic-year-modification
rules.description: A field that represents a year is being modified by an arithmetic operation, but no proper check for leap years can be detected afterwards.

rules.name: cpp/missing-check-scanf
rules.description: Failing to check that a call to 'scanf' actually writes to an output variable can lead to unexpected behavior at reading time.

rules.name: cpp/allocation-too-small
rules.description: Calling 'malloc', 'calloc' or 'realloc' without allocating enough memory to contain an instance of the type of the pointer may result in a buffer overflow

rules.name: cpp/suspicious-allocation-size
rules.description: Calling 'malloc', 'calloc' or 'realloc' without allocating enough memory to contain multiple instances of the type of the pointer may result in a buffer overflow

rules.name: cpp/telemetry/succeeded-includes
rules.description: A count of all succeeded includes, grouped by filename.

rules.name: cpp/telemetry/compiler-errors
rules.description: A count of all compiler errors, grouped by error text.

rules.name: cpp/telemetry/extraction-information
rules.description: Information about the extraction for a C/C++ database

rules.name: cpp/telemetry/database-quality
rules.description: Metrics that indicate the quality of the database.

rules.name: cpp/telemetry/failed-includes
rules.description: A count of all failed includes, grouped by filename.

rules.name: cpp/telemetry/extraction-metrics
rules.description: Raw metrics relating to extraction.

rules.name: cpp/summary/lines-of-user-code
rules.description: The total number of lines of C/C++ code from the source code directory, excluding auto-generated files. This query counts the lines of code, excluding whitespace or comments. Note: If external libraries are included in the codebase either in a checked-in virtual environment or as vendored code, that will currently be counted as user written code.

rules.name: cpp/summary/lines-of-code
rules.description: The total number of lines of C/C++ code across all files, including system headers, libraries, and auto-generated files. This is a useful metric of the size of a database. For all files that were seen during the build, this query counts the lines of code, excluding whitespace or comments.
